en.question: Which is an example of a deterministic guardrail as opposed to a probabilistic one?

options.text: A code check that blocks responses matching a card-number pattern.
A system prompt instructing the model to refuse requests for medical advice.
options.note: Instructions strongly influence behaviour but can be circumvented.

options.text: A few-shot example demonstrating how a refusal should be worded.
Selecting a more capable model tier that refuses unsafe requests more often.
options.note: Capability reduces error rates without providing any guarantee.

en.explanation: A deterministic guardrail is code that always executes and returns the same decision for the same input. It either fires or does not, without depending on the model choosing to comply.
